claims: A moderate (G2) to strong (G3) geomagnetic storm is expected to impact Earth through March 20–21, 2026.
The expected moderate (G2) to strong (G3) geomagnetic storm is due to multiple Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs).
Geomagnetic storms are caused by solar winds, solar flares, and Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs).
Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) are massive explosions of plasma and magnetic fields from the Sun.
NOAA classifies geomagnetic storms on a G-scale from G1 (minor) to G5 (extreme).
The 1859 Carrington Event is the most intense geomagnetic storm on record.
The 1859 Carrington Event disrupted telegraph systems.
In 1989, a geomagnetic storm caused a major power blackout in Quebec, Canada.
In March 2026, the Sun is in a high-activity phase of its 11-year cycle.
The Sun's 11-year cycle high-activity phase is projected to continue through 2027.
A G4 (severe) geomagnetic storm was recorded on January 19, 2026.
The G4 (severe) geomagnetic storm on January 19, 2026 followed an X-class solar flare.
